subject: community-medicine
title: Cancer epidemiology and control: registries, screening and warning signs

steps.tx: A **cancer registry** is an organisation that systematically collects, stores, analyses and reports data on people with cancer. There are two main types. A **hospital based registry** records all patients seen by one institution, inpatients and outpatients alike. A **population based registry** covers every case within a defined geographic area and gives true incidence rates. The optimum base population for a population based registry is 2 to 7 million.

steps.tx: The **National Cancer Control Programme** was launched in 1975-76 with the aims of prevention, early diagnosis and treatment. Under it, government hospitals and government medical colleges received a grant of Rs 3.00 crores to develop an oncology wing. Population based registries help assess how well such control programmes are working and measure the burden of disease.

steps.tx: Two **HPV vaccines** are available in India against cervical cancer. The quadrivalent vaccine, Gardasil, covers HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18. The bivalent vaccine, Cervarix, covers types 16 and 18. Types 16 and 18 cause about 70 percent of cervical cancers, while types 6 and 11 cause about 90 percent of anogenital warts. Neither vaccine gives complete protection, so screening continues.

steps.tx: Watch for **warning signs** of cancer. These include a lump or hard area in the breast, a change in a wart or mole, a persistent change in bowel habit, a persistent cough or hoarseness, unexplained loss of weight, blood loss from any natural orifice, and a swelling or sore that does not heal. Unexplained weight gain is not a warning sign, so it is the answer when asked which item is the exception.
